abstract: The lecture describes the anatomy of the larynx: its situation and extent from C4 to C6, its nine cartilages, joints, ligaments and membranes, the intrinsic and extrinsic muscles and their actions on the vocal cords, its internal compartments, histology, relations, blood supply, lymphatic drainage and innervation. It then covers the physiology of phonation and clinical correlations, including recurrent and external laryngeal nerve damage, laryngeal obstruction and vocal nodules.

concepts.name: Larynx
concepts.definition: The upper expanded part of the lower respiratory tract, modified for producing voice. It is an unpaired median tube of cartilages linked by joints, muscles and ligaments, extending from C4 to C6, that acts as a sphincter at the inlet of the lower respiratory tract; its functions are phonation, respiration, protection and deglutition.

evidence.quote: The larynx is the upper expanded part of the lower respiratory tract, modified for producing voice, also called the organ of phonation
It acts as a sphincter at the inlet of lower respiratory tract to protect the trachea and the bronchial tree
Larynx extends from the upper thyroid cartilage at C4 to the lower cricoid at C6

concepts.name: Laryngeal cartilage
concepts.definition: One of the nine cartilages of the larynx: three unpaired and large (thyroid, cricoid, epiglottis) and three paired and small (arytenoid, corniculate, cuneiform). The principal ones are the cricoid, the thyroid and the two arytenoids.

evidence.quote: Nine cartilages. Three unpaired and large: thyroid, cricoid, epiglottis. Three paired and small: arytenoid, corniculate, cuneiform.
The larynx is composed of nine cartilages, of which three are unpaired and three are paired

concepts.name: Thyroid cartilage
concepts.definition: A large unpaired laryngeal cartilage shaped like an open book, open backwards, with two vertical quadrilateral laminae and superior and inferior cornua, the inferior carrying a cricoid articular surface. Its upper border, at the body of C4, marks the superior extent of the larynx.

evidence.quote: Shaped like an open book, open backwards, with two vertical quadrilateral laminae
Superior: upper border of the thyroid cartilage, at the level of the body of C4

concepts.name: Laryngeal prominence
concepts.definition: The forward bulge, also called the Adam's apple, formed where the two laminae of the thyroid cartilage meet in the midline.

evidence.quote: formed where the two laminae of the thyroid cartilage meet in the midline

concepts.name: Cricoid cartilage
concepts.definition: An unpaired signet-shaped ring of cartilage with a narrow anterior arch and a broad posterior lamina, at the level of C6. It is the only cartilage that completely encircles the lumen of the larynx and is called the foundation stone of the larynx.

evidence.quote: A signet-shaped ring with a narrow anterior arch and a broad posterior lamina, at C6
The cricoid is the only complete ring in the airway, at C6, the foundation stone of the larynx.
The cricoid cartilage is situated at the level of C6 vertebra and completely encircles the lumen of the larynx

concepts.name: Epiglottis
concepts.definition: An unpaired laryngeal cartilage shaped like a tennis racket, with a free superior base and an inferior foot that inserts into the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage through the thyroepiglottic ligament. Its posterior (laryngeal) side faces the vestibule and its anterior (lingual) side faces the base of the tongue and the hyoid.

evidence.quote: Shaped like a tennis racket with a curved lower handle forming its foot
Shape: tennis racket with curved lower handle forming the foot of the epiglottis

concepts.name: Arytenoid cartilage
concepts.definition: A paired laryngeal cartilage shaped like a triangular pyramid about 15 mm high. Its apex articulates with the corniculate cartilage and its concave base with the cricoid lamina; the base carries the vocal process anteriorly and the muscular process laterally.

evidence.quote: Triangular pyramids about 15 mm high. The apex articulates with the corniculate cartilage, the concave base with the cricoid lamina
The anterior angle of the base is extended by the vocal process

concepts.name: Vocal process of the arytenoid cartilage
concepts.definition: The extension of the anterior angle of the base of the arytenoid cartilage, which gives insertion to the vocal ligament.

evidence.quote: The anterior angle of the base extends as the vocal process (insertion of the vocal ligament)
The vocal process gives insertion to the : • Vocal ligament

concepts.name: Muscular process of the arytenoid cartilage
concepts.definition: The process on the lateral angle of the base of the arytenoid cartilage, on which the posterior and lateral cricoarytenoid muscles insert.

evidence.quote: the lateral angle bears the muscular process (insertion of the posterior and lateral cricoarytenoid muscles)
The lateral angle presents the muscular process on which insert

concepts.name: Corniculate cartilage
concepts.definition: A small paired accessory cartilage of the larynx that rests on the apex of the arytenoid cartilage.

evidence.quote: Corniculate: on the apices of the arytenoids

concepts.name: Cuneiform cartilage
concepts.definition: A small paired accessory cartilage of the larynx lying in the aryepiglottic fold.

evidence.quote: Cuneiform: in the aryepiglottic fold

concepts.name: Hyoid bone
concepts.definition: The U-shaped bone above the larynx, closely associated with the larynx but usually considered a separate structure. The larynx is united to it by muscles and ligaments.

evidence.quote: Hyoid bone: the U-shaped bone above the larynx.
It is closely associated with the larynx but is usually considered a separate structure
Above: the hyoid bone and base of the tongue

concepts.name: Trachea
concepts.definition: The tube of C-shaped cartilage rings below the cricoid cartilage, with which the larynx is continuous inferiorly.

evidence.quote: Trachea: the tube of C-shaped cartilage rings below the cricoid.
Above: the hyoid bone and base of the tongue. Below: the trachea

concepts.name: Cricoarytenoid joint
concepts.definition: The functionally most important joint of the larynx: an elliptical synovial articulation uniting the base of the arytenoid with the upper edge of the cricoid lamina. Its rotatory movement abducts or adducts the vocal cords and its gliding movement closes or opens the posterior part of the glottis.

evidence.quote: An elliptical synovial articulation reinforced by the posterior cricoarytenoid ligament, uniting the base of the arytenoid with the upper edge of the cricoid lamina
Cricoarytenoid joint: rotation abducts and adducts; gliding opens and closes the posterior glottis.
Rotatory movement, in which arytenoid cartilage moves around a vertical axis, thus abducting or adducting the vocal cords

concepts.name: Cricothyroid joint
concepts.definition: A flat synovial joint joining the lower cornu of the thyroid cartilage and the lateral face of the cricoid. Tilting of the cricoid around a transverse axis at this joint tenses the vocal cords.

evidence.quote: A flat synovial joint reinforced by ligaments, joining the lower cornu of the thyroid cartilage and the lateral face of the cricoid
Cricothyroid joint: tilting tenses the vocal cords.
Movements: tilting of the cricoid around a transverse axis inducing a tension of the vocal cords

concepts.name: Thyrohyoid membrane
concepts.definition: An extrinsic membrane of the larynx running from the upper edge of the thyroid cartilage to the lower edge of the hyoid bone, with a medial and two lateral thickenings. It is pierced by the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve with the superior laryngeal artery.

evidence.quote: Thyrohyoid membrane: from the upper edge of the thyroid cartilage to the lower edge of the hyoid bone
The internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve pierces it with the superior laryngeal artery

concepts.name: Thyroepiglottic ligament
concepts.definition: An extrinsic ligament that attaches the lower narrow end (foot) of the epiglottis to the posterior surface of the thyroid angle.

evidence.quote: Thyroepiglottic ligament: attaches the lower narrow end of the epiglottis to the posterior surface of the thyroid angle
inferior inserts into the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage through the thyroepiglottic ligament

concepts.name: Hyoepiglottic ligament
concepts.definition: An extrinsic ligament connecting the posterior aspect of the hyoid with the anterior surface of the upper end of the epiglottis.

evidence.quote: Hyoepiglottic ligament: connects the posterior aspect of the hyoid with the anterior surface of the upper end of the epiglottis

concepts.name: Cricotracheal ligament
concepts.definition: An extrinsic ligament between the lower edge of the cricoid and the upper edge of the first tracheal ring, connecting the larynx to the trachea.

evidence.quote: Cricotracheal ligament: between the lower edge of the cricoid and the upper edge of the first tracheal ring

concepts.name: Cricothyroid ligament
concepts.definition: The fibroelastic ligament between the thyroid and cricoid cartilages. Stretched between the thyroid cartilage and the vocal process it forms the vocal ligament, and with the cricoid it surrounds the infraglottic cavity; its median part lies just under the skin and is where an emergency airway is made.

evidence.quote: The cricothyroid ligament, stretched between the thyroid cartilage and the vocal process, forms the vocal ligament
The median cricothyroid ligament sits just under the skin between two easily felt landmarks, the thyroid cartilage above and the cricoid below
surrounded by the cricoid and the cricothyroid ligament

concepts.name: Vocal ligament
concepts.definition: An intrinsic ligament formed by the cricothyroid ligament stretched between the thyroid cartilage and the vocal process of the arytenoid. Together with muscle it makes up the vocal cord.

evidence.quote: The cricothyroid ligament, stretched between the thyroid cartilage and the vocal process, forms the vocal ligament
Made up of vocal ligament and muscle

concepts.name: Vestibular ligament
concepts.definition: An intrinsic ligament of the larynx stretched between the thyroid angle and the anterolateral aspect of the arytenoid.

evidence.quote: The vestibular ligament is tense between the thyroid angle and the anterolateral aspect of the arytenoid

concepts.name: Intrinsic laryngeal muscle
concepts.definition: A muscle of the larynx itself, classified by action as a tensor of the vocal cord, the dilator of the glottis or a constrictor of the glottis. All are paired except the transverse arytenoid, and all are supplied by the recurrent laryngeal nerve except the cricothyroid.

evidence.quote: All the intrinsic muscles are paired except the transverse arytenoid (interarytenoid), which is unpaired
Recurrent laryngeal nerve supplies all intrinsic muscles except the cricothyroid

concepts.name: Posterior cricoarytenoid muscle
concepts.definition: The intrinsic laryngeal muscle that inserts on the muscular process of the arytenoid and is the only abductor of the vocal cords (the only dilator of the glottis). It is called the safety muscle of the larynx because, if it is paralysed, the adductors take the upper hand and the person might die from lack of air.

evidence.quote: The posterior cricoarytenoids are the only intrinsic muscles that abduct the vocal cords, letting air through the rima glottidis
Posterior cricoarytenoids are the only abductors: the safety muscles of the larynx.
If posterior cricoarytenoids are paralyzed, the adductor muscles (of vocal cords) take the upper hand and the person might die due to lack of air

concepts.name: Lateral cricoarytenoid muscle
concepts.definition: An intrinsic laryngeal muscle that inserts on the muscular process of the arytenoid and adducts the vocal cords; it is one of the constrictors of the glottis.

evidence.quote: Adduct the vocal cords | Lateral cricoarytenoids, transverse arytenoid
2. Lateral cricoarytenoids: adduct the vocal cords.

concepts.name: Transverse arytenoid muscle
concepts.definition: The only unpaired intrinsic muscle of the larynx, inserting on the posterior side of the arytenoid cartilages. It adducts the vocal cords.

evidence.quote: Transverse arytenoid is the only unpaired intrinsic muscle.
All the intrinsic muscles are paired except the transverse arytenoid (interarytenoid), which is unpaired
3. Transverse arytenoid: adduct the vocal cords.

concepts.name: Cricothyroid muscle
concepts.definition: A paired intrinsic muscle that tenses the vocal cord by elevating the cricoid arch and lowering the thyroid cartilage. It is the only muscle lying on the outer aspect of the larynx and the only one supplied by the external laryngeal nerve; it is important for the tone and pitch of the voice.

evidence.quote: Vocal cord tensors: cricothyroid (paired). Action: elevation of the cricoid arch and lowering of the thyroid cartilage, tensing the vocal cord
Cricothyroid is the only muscle on the outer aspect and the only one on the external laryngeal nerve.
The cricothyroid is important for the tone and pitch of the voice

concepts.name: Vocalis muscle
concepts.definition: The inferior thyroarytenoid or vocal muscle, running from the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage to the anterolateral aspect of the arytenoid. It tilts the arytenoid forward and tenses the vocal cord.

evidence.quote: inferior thyroarytenoid or vocal muscle (from the reentrant angle to the anterolateral aspect of the arytenoid), which tilts the arytenoid forward and tenses the cord
Tense: cricothyroid and vocalis.

concepts.name: Thyroarytenoid muscle
concepts.definition: An intrinsic laryngeal muscle arising from the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage and passing to the arytenoid, listed among the constrictors of the glottis. It relaxes the vocal cords.

evidence.quote: Relax the vocal cords | Thyroarytenoid
superior thyroarytenoid (from the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage to the lower third of the arytenoid)
3. Thyroarytenoid: relaxes the vocal cords

concepts.name: Extrinsic laryngeal muscle
concepts.definition: A muscle that moves the larynx as a whole, ensuring laryngeal mobility especially during swallowing. The elevators are the thyrohyoid, mylohyoid and digastric; the depressors are the sternothyroid, sternohyoid and omohyoid.

evidence.quote: Extrinsic muscles ensure laryngeal mobility, especially during swallowing. Elevators: thyrohyoid, mylohyoid, digastric. Depressors: sternothyroid, sternohyoid, omohyoid
Extrinsic muscles: ensure laryngeal mobility especially during swallowing

concepts.name: Vocal cord abduction
concepts.definition: The movement that opens the glottis and lets air through the rima glottidis. The muscular processes of both arytenoids rotate medially and the vocal processes rotate laterally, giving a wide diamond-shaped opening; it is produced only by the posterior cricoarytenoid muscles.

evidence.quote: When they contract, the muscular processes of both arytenoids rotate medially and the vocal processes rotate laterally, giving a wide diamond-shaped opening
Abduct the vocal cords | Posterior cricoarytenoids

concepts.name: Vocal cord adduction
concepts.definition: The movement that brings the vocal cords together and closes the glottis, produced by the lateral cricoarytenoids and the transverse arytenoid. The cords are kept adducted at the start of phonation.

evidence.quote: Adduct the vocal cords | Lateral cricoarytenoids, transverse arytenoid
The vocal cords are kept adducted

concepts.name: Vocal cord tensing
concepts.definition: The increase in tension of the vocal cords, produced by the cricothyroid and the vocalis and by tilting of the cricoid at the cricothyroid joint. It makes the cord ready to vibrate.

evidence.quote: Tense the vocal cords | Cricothyroid, vocalis
Tilting of the cricoid around a transverse axis (arch up, lamina down) tenses the vocal cords

concepts.name: Supraglottic compartment of the larynx
concepts.definition: The part of the larynx above the glottis, comprising the vestibule, the laryngeal (Morgagni) ventricle and the interarytenoid region. Its lymphatics are very rich and drain to the internal jugular chain.

evidence.quote: Supraglottic | Vestibule: a pyramidal space from the laryngeal margin to the ventricular bands
Very rich in the supraglottic zone, thinner in the subglottic zone, absent at the vocal cords

concepts.name: Vestibule of the larynx
concepts.definition: A pyramidal space of the supraglottic compartment extending from the laryngeal margin to the ventricular bands, that is, the space above the vestibular folds.

evidence.quote: Vestibule: a pyramidal space from the laryngeal margin to the ventricular bands
Spaces: vestibule above the vestibular folds, ventricle between them and the vocal folds, infraglottic cavity below.

concepts.name: Laryngeal ventricle
concepts.definition: The cavity between the ventricular bands (false vocal cords) above and the plane of the vocal cords below.

evidence.quote: Laryngeal or Morgagni ventricle: between the ventricular bands (false vocal cords) above and the plane of the vocal cords below
ventricle between them and the vocal folds

concepts.name: Vestibular fold
concepts.definition: The false vocal cord or ventricular band, which lies above the laryngeal ventricle; the vestibule of the larynx is the space above the vestibular folds.

evidence.quote: between the ventricular bands (false vocal cords) above and the plane of the vocal cords below
vestibule above the vestibular folds, ventricle between them and the vocal folds

concepts.name: Glottis
concepts.definition: The compartment of the larynx formed by the two vocal cords and the triangular opening they delimit, narrower than the vestibular cleft. It is a narrow zone in children, where obstructive oedema causes respiratory distress very rapidly.

evidence.quote: The glottis is triangular and narrower than the vestibular cleft: a narrow zone in children, where obstructive oedema causes respiratory distress very rapidly
Glottis: delimited by the 2 vocal cords, it is triangular in shape

concepts.name: Vocal cord
concepts.definition: One of two pearly white cords stretched between the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage in front and the arytenoid behind, made of vocal ligament and muscle. Its epithelium is non-keratinized stratified squamous and it has no lymphatics.

evidence.quote: Two pearly white vocal cords stretched between the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage in front and the arytenoid behind, made of vocal ligament and muscle
Vocal cords: 2 pearly white cords stretched between the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage in front and the arytenoid cartilage in back
Vocal cords have stratified squamous epithelium and no lymphatics

concepts.name: Anterior commissure of the larynx
concepts.definition: The point where the two vocal cords unite anteriorly, attached directly to the thyroid cartilage and containing vessels and lymphatics.

evidence.quote: Anteriorly they unite at the anterior commissure, attached directly to the thyroid cartilage and containing vessels and lymphatics
unite to form the Anterior Commissure, directly attached to the thyroid cartilage containing vessels and lymphatics

concepts.name: Infraglottic cavity
concepts.definition: The cavity of the larynx below the vocal cords, surrounded by the cricoid and the cricothyroid ligament.

evidence.quote: Infraglottic | The cavity below the vocal cords, surrounded by the cricoid and the cricothyroid ligament
Infraglottic cavity — space inferior to vocal folds

concepts.name: Laryngeal mucosa
concepts.definition: The thin, smooth, pale pink lining of the larynx, continuous above with the pharyngeal mucosa and below with the tracheal mucosa. Its epithelium is respiratory type throughout, except at the vocal cords and the upper half of the epiglottis, where it is non-keratinized stratified squamous.

evidence.quote: The epithelium is respiratory type (cylindric stratified) throughout, except at the vocal cords and the upper half of the epiglottis, which are non-keratinized stratified squamous
Epithelium is respiratory except at the vocal cords and upper half of the epiglottis: stratified squamous.
Non-keratinized stratified squamous type at the vocal cords and the upper

concepts.name: Superior laryngeal artery
concepts.definition: A branch of the superior thyroid artery that supplies the supraglottic part of the larynx and anastomoses with the posteroinferior laryngeal artery. It enters the larynx with the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve through the thyrohyoid membrane.

evidence.quote: Superior laryngeal artery | A branch of the superior thyroid artery. Supplies the supraglottic part and anastomoses with the posteroinferior laryngeal artery
Superior Laryngeal Artery (SLA): branch of the Superior Thyroid Artery, it vascularizes the supraglottic part and anastomoses with ALPI

concepts.name: Anteroinferior laryngeal artery
concepts.definition: A branch of the superior thyroid artery that supplies the anterior part of the infraglottic stage of the larynx.

evidence.quote: Anteroinferior laryngeal artery | A branch of the superior thyroid artery. Supplies the anterior part of the infraglottic stage
Anteroinferior Laryngeal Artery (ALAI): branch of the Superior Thyroid Artery, it vascularizes the anterior part of the infraglottic stage

concepts.name: Posteroinferior laryngeal artery
concepts.definition: A branch of the inferior thyroid artery that supplies the posterior part of the laryngeal mucosa and anastomoses with the superior laryngeal artery.

evidence.quote: Posteroinferior laryngeal artery | A branch of the inferior thyroid artery. Supplies the posterior part of the laryngeal mucosa
Posteroinferior Laryngeal Artery (ALPI): branch of the Inferior Thyroid Artery. It vascularizes the posterior part of the laryngeal mucosa

concepts.name: Superior thyroid artery
concepts.definition: The artery that gives off the superior laryngeal artery and the anteroinferior laryngeal artery. Its ligation is a setting for external laryngeal nerve injury.

evidence.quote: Superior laryngeal artery | A branch of the superior thyroid artery
External laryngeal injury (superior thyroid artery ligation)

concepts.name: Inferior thyroid artery
concepts.definition: The artery that gives off the posteroinferior laryngeal artery.

evidence.quote: Posteroinferior laryngeal artery | A branch of the inferior thyroid artery

concepts.name: Venous drainage of the larynx
concepts.definition: The laryngeal veins are satellite to the arteries. The superior and inferior laryngeal veins drain to the superior thyroid vein, then the thyro-linguo-facial trunk and the internal jugular vein; the posterior laryngeal vein drains to the inferior thyroid vein and then the subclavian vein.

evidence.quote: Superior and inferior laryngeal veins to the superior thyroid vein, then the thyro-linguo-facial trunk, then the internal jugular vein
Venous: satellite to the arteries Internal jugular vein and subclavian vein

concepts.name: Lymphatic drainage of the larynx
concepts.definition: The lymphatics of the larynx are very rich in the supraglottic zone, thinner in the subglottic zone and absent at the vocal cords. The supraglottic region drains to the internal jugular chain; the infraglottic region drains to pretracheal and paratracheal nodes and the internal jugular chain.

evidence.quote: Very rich in the supraglottic zone, thinner in the subglottic zone, absent at the vocal cords
Lymphatics are absent at the vocal cords, rich supraglottically.
Lymphatic: Very rich in the supraglottic zones, thinner in the subglottic zone, absent in the vocal cords

concepts.name: Internal jugular lymph node chain
concepts.definition: The chain of lymph nodes that receives the lymphatic drainage of the supraglottic region and, together with pretracheal and paratracheal nodes, of the infraglottic region of the larynx.

evidence.quote: Supraglottic: the internal jugular chain. Infraglottic: pretracheal and paratracheal nodes and the internal jugular chain
Supraglottic region → internal jugular chain

concepts.name: Vagus nerve
concepts.definition: The nerve whose branches, the superior laryngeal nerve and the recurrent laryngeal nerve, innervate the larynx.

evidence.quote: A branch of the vagus, mixed but essentially sensory
From the vagus, on the right at the base of the neck and on the left at the thorax

concepts.name: Superior laryngeal nerve
concepts.definition: A branch of the vagus, mixed but essentially sensory, that descends against the pharyngeal wall and divides behind the greater horn of the hyoid into an internal and an external branch.

evidence.quote: A branch of the vagus, mixed but essentially sensory, descending against the pharyngeal wall and dividing behind the greater horn of the hyoid
It divides behind the greater horn of the hyoid into two branches

concepts.name: Internal laryngeal nerve
aliases: Internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve
concepts.definition: The internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve. It enters the larynx with the superior laryngeal artery by piercing the thyrohyoid membrane and gives sensory innervation to the mucosa above the vocal folds, plus autonomic fibres.

evidence.quote: Internal branch | Enters the larynx with the superior laryngeal artery by perforating the thyrohyoid membrane. Sensory innervation of the supraglottic mucosa, plus autonomic fibres
Internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve: sensation above the cords, piercing the thyrohyoid membrane.
Pierces thyrohyoid membrane + Sensory from mucosa above vocal folds

concepts.name: External laryngeal nerve
aliases: External branch of the superior laryngeal nerve
concepts.definition: The external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve. It innervates the cricothyroid muscle and perforates the cricothyroid membrane, and is described as giving sensory innervation to the subglottic stage.

evidence.quote: External branch | Innervates the cricothyroid muscle and perforates the cricothyroid membrane; sensory innervation of the subglottic stage
External branch - innervates cricothyroid m

concepts.name: Recurrent laryngeal nerve
concepts.definition: A branch of the vagus arising on the right at the base of the neck and on the left in the thorax. It is motor to all the intrinsic muscles of the larynx except the cricothyroid and sensory below the vocal folds.

evidence.quote: Motor to all the intrinsic muscles except the cricothyroid; sensory below the vocal folds through an ascending branch anastomosing with the superior laryngeal nerve
Recurrent laryngeal nerve supplies all intrinsic muscles except the cricothyroid, and sensation below the cords.
Recurrent laryngeal n. + Motor to intrinsic muscles of larynx (except

concepts.name: Galen's loop
concepts.definition: The anastomosis formed by an ascending sensory branch of the recurrent laryngeal nerve with the superior laryngeal nerve.

evidence.quote: through an ascending branch anastomosing with the superior laryngeal nerve: Galen's loop

concepts.name: Phonation
concepts.definition: The set of mechanisms allowing vibration at the free edge of the vocal fold, transforming aerodynamic energy into acoustic energy. The adducted cords are opened by infraglottic air pressure, vibrate as air passes, and the sound is then modified by the supralaryngeal cavities.

evidence.quote: The set of mechanisms allowing vibration at the free edge of the vocal fold, transforming aerodynamic energy into acoustic energy
The phonation (speech) is produced by the vibrations of the vocal cords

concepts.name: Vibratory cycle of the vocal folds
concepts.definition: The three-step cycle of phonation: the folds close as the arytenoids come together (phonatory position); they open when the subglottic pressure overcomes the muscular and elastic resistance, letting a puff of air pass; then the folds close again.

evidence.quote: Putting into phonatory position: the folds close as the arytenoids come together. 2. Opening: when the subglottic pressure overcomes the muscular and elastic resistance

concepts.name: Acoustic parameters of the voice
concepts.definition: The three parameters that characterise the voice: frequency, in Hertz, depending on the vibration speed of the vocal folds; intensity, in dB, depending on the force of pulmonary expiration (subglottic pressure); and pitch, depending on the accommodation of the vocal folds and especially on the shape of the supralaryngeal cavities.

evidence.quote: The voice is characterised by three acoustic parameters: frequency, in Hertz, depending on the vibration speed of the vocal folds
Voice parameters: frequency (Hz), intensity (dB), pitch.
The voice is characterized by 3 acoustic parameters

concepts.name: Subglottic pressure
concepts.definition: The air pressure below the glottis created by the expiratory blow from the lungs. It overcomes the resistance of the vocal cords to open them and determines the intensity of the voice.

evidence.quote: The expiratory blow creates a subglottic pressure that overcomes the resistance of the vocal cords
intensity, in dB, depending on the force of pulmonary expiration (subglottic pressure)

concepts.name: Supralaryngeal cavity
concepts.definition: One of the air cavities above the larynx that modify and filter the laryngeal sound into vowels and consonants. They have a filter role (resonance, with the pharynx and oral cavity as areas of particular enhancement) and an articulation role.

evidence.quote: The sound produced is immediately modified and filtered by the supralaryngeal air cavities to become vowels and consonants: the bucco-pharyngeal resonators
Filter role: resonance and enrichment of certain frequencies or suppression of others, with two areas of particular enhancement, the pharynx and the oral cavity

concepts.name: Recurrent laryngeal nerve injury
concepts.definition: Damage to the recurrent laryngeal nerve, often accidental during partial thyroidectomy. Unilaterally, the cord lies in the paramedian position and does not vibrate, though the other usually compensates; bilaterally, both cords lie paramedian with loss of phonation and difficulty breathing.

evidence.quote: Recurrent laryngeal nerve, often damaged accidentally during partial thyroidectomy: unilaterally, the cord lies in the paramedian position and does not vibrate
Unilateral recurrent nerve palsy: paramedian cord.
Bilateral: stridor, airway emergency

concepts.name: External laryngeal nerve injury
concepts.definition: Damage to the external laryngeal nerve, which causes weakness of phonation from loss of the tightening effect of the cricothyroid: a weak, monotone voice, especially noticeable in singers.

evidence.quote: External laryngeal nerve: weakness of phonation from loss of the tightening effect of the cricothyroid
External laryngeal injury (superior thyroid artery ligation): weak, monotone voice, can't reach high notes

concepts.name: Paramedian position of the vocal cord
concepts.definition: The position of a vocal cord between abduction and adduction, in which it does not vibrate; it is the position of the cord after recurrent laryngeal nerve damage.

evidence.quote: Unilateral damage leaves the cord on the affected side in the paramedian position, between abduction and adduction, not vibrating
lies in paramedian position (between ‘abduction and adduction) and does not vibrate

concepts.name: Cadaveric position of the vocal cords
concepts.definition: The position of the vocal cords, further abducted and fixed, when both the recurrent and the external laryngeal nerves are damaged on both sides and all the intrinsic muscles are paralysed.

evidence.quote: all the intrinsic muscles are paralysed and the cords are further abducted and fixed: the cadaveric position
Bilateral with external nerve: cadaveric position.
This is known as the cadaveric postion of vocal cords

concepts.name: Hoarseness
concepts.definition: A hoarse voice, the sign of unilateral recurrent laryngeal palsy; it can be caused by thyroidectomy or by a lung or mediastinal mass acting on the long left recurrent nerve.

evidence.quote: Unilateral recurrent laryngeal palsy (thyroidectomy, left-sided aortic or lung lesions): hoarse voice, cord paramedian
The long left course is why a lung or mediastinal mass can cause hoarseness

concepts.name: Thyroidectomy
concepts.definition: An operation during which the recurrent laryngeal nerve is often damaged accidentally.

evidence.quote: Recurrent laryngeal nerve, often damaged accidentally during partial thyroidectomy

concepts.name: Vocal nodule
concepts.definition: An inflammatory nodule that develops in people who overuse the voice, at the junction of the anterior one third and posterior two thirds of the vocal cords, the area of maximum contact during vibration. The nodules are bilateral and symmetrical, soft, reddish and oedematous early and later greyish or whitish.

evidence.quote: People who overuse the voice develop inflammatory nodules there: bilateral, symmetrical, from pin head to split pea in size
Vocal nodules form at the junction of the anterior third and posterior two thirds of the cords.
During vibration the area of maximum contact between the vocal Cords is at the junction of their anterior one-third

concepts.name: Laryngeal obstruction
concepts.definition: Obstruction of the larynx by a foreign body. The mucosa of the superior larynx is very sensitive, so a foreign body normally causes immediate explosive coughing; if that reflex is slowed or absent, choking follows.

evidence.quote: The mucosa of the superior larynx is very sensitive, so a foreign body causes immediate explosive coughing. If that reflex is slowed or absent, choking follows

concepts.name: Heimlich manoeuvre
concepts.definition: A manoeuvre to relieve choking: standing behind the victim with the hands in front of the epigastrium, one as a fist and the other over it, three or four abdominal thrusts directed upwards and backwards squeeze the residual air up to dislodge the foreign body.

evidence.quote: then give three or four abdominal thrusts directed upwards and backwards, squeezing the residual air up to dislodge the foreign body
The Heimlich manoeuvre relieves it

concepts.name: Laryngeal cancer
concepts.definition: A tumour of the larynx whose spread depends on the lymphatics of its compartment: a tumour confined to the vocal cord spreads late and has a good outlook, while a supraglottic tumour reaches the internal jugular nodes early.

evidence.quote: glottic cancer spreads late (good prognosis); supraglottic cancer spreads early
A tumour confined to the cord spreads late and has a good outlook

concepts.name: Cricothyroidotomy

notes: The packet contains no list of known concepts, so all concept names were chosen from the packet's own wording.

Slides 37 and 64 are heavily garbled by OCR (missing words, misspellings such as 'postion', 'ericoarytenoids', 'Vocals'); slide quotes were copied as they appear. Slide 53 is only a dump of figure labels and was not used.

The packet uses 'cricothyroid ligament', 'median cricothyroid ligament' and 'cricothyroid membrane' for what appears to be the same structure; they were merged into one concept (Cricothyroid ligament) with medium confidence.

'Vocalis' in the action table and 'inferior thyroarytenoid or vocal muscle' in the classification were treated as the same muscle (Vocalis muscle); the packet does not state this equivalence in one place. The thyroarytenoid is listed both as a constrictor of the glottis and as the muscle that relaxes the cords.
Glottis and rima glottidis are treated as one concept because the question on the rima glottidis is explained using the glottis.

Question q:1g9vm87 words the nodule site as the 'junction of anterior and middle thirds' in its option comment, while the text says 'anterior one third and posterior two thirds'; these describe the same point, so it is not listed as a conflict.
The laryngeal prominence is supported only by question and flashcard blocks (no summary section or slide text mentions it).
The summary names the thickenings of the thyrohyoid membrane 'medial thyroid ligament' and 'lateral thyroid ligaments'; no separate concepts were made for them.

The pretracheal and paratracheal nodes, the aortic arch and subclavian artery (course of the recurrent nerves, hy:7), the piriform sinus and the individual extrinsic muscles are mentioned in the packet but were not given their own concepts.
